findings.evidence: features/005-scope-change-skill/005-scope-change-skill-prd.md:R2 + R7.1 + Open questions §1 — R2 specifies that `specflow:develop` Phase F.3 (Verifier rejection, option 3) and Phase A's resume prompt (option 3) emit a y/n prompt to invoke `specflow:scope-change`. R7.1 specifies that tasks with `task-history.json.status == in_progress` are NOT auto-regenerated and surface to the impact list. Open questions §1 explicitly notes the unsettled case: scope change affects R3 but `specflow:develop` is currently mid-run on a task anchored to R5 (an unaffected R-ID) — recommended 'proceed in parallel'. But R2 trigger (a) (Verifier rejection option 3) is BY DEFINITION mid-run — the Verifier just rejected the AI's claim and the user picked option 3; `specflow:develop` is paused at the rejection point, not exited. If the user accepts the y/n prompt and `specflow:scope-change` fires, the in-flight `specflow:develop` run's state is undefined: does the user's `specflow:develop` shell session exit cleanly when scope-change fires? Does scope-change's step (i) interview extension write into the same `admin/scratch/` namespace that `specflow:develop` is using? Does the impact-list step (vi) see the in-flight task as `in_progress` (per R7.1) and surface IT as the artefact triggering the scope-change to begin with — a circular reference (the task that triggered scope-change appears in its own impact list)?
findings.claim: Cross-cutting concern (cross-skill state contamination) — the integration surface between `specflow:develop` and `specflow:scope-change` is named (R2 trigger paths) but the in-flight execution state across the two skills' lifecycles is not. The PRD covers (scope-change-fires-after-develop-pauses) implicitly via R2 + R7.1 but doesn't name (a) what happens to `specflow:develop`'s scratch state when scope-change fires from inside a Verifier-rejection moment; (b) whether the task that just got rejected appears in scope-change's own impact list (and if so, with what recommended action — the user just chose to scope-change because of it, so 'consider rebasing' would be tautological); (c) whether scope-change's step (viii) cleanup signals back to the paused `specflow:develop` run that it should resume against the new PRD/tasks or exit cleanly. Phase 2's `specflow:develop` Phase F.3 names option 3 as 'abort the task and surface to scope-change' — 'abort' suggests develop exits, but the cleanup-and-handoff contract is not specified in either skill's PRD.
findings.proposed_change: Extend R2 with a state-handoff clause and extend R8 (impact list) with a self-reference exclusion clause. Concrete edits: (a) R2 addition: 'When trigger (a) (Verifier rejection option 3) fires, `specflow:develop` exits cleanly before the y/n prompt — the in-flight task's `task-history.json.status` is updated to `aborted_for_scope_change` (a new status value distinct from `in_progress` so R7.1 partial-completion handling does NOT misclassify the aborted task as in-flight); the `specflow:develop` scratch directory is preserved (not cleaned) so the user can resume after scope-change closes. After scope-change step (viii) cleanup, the user re-invokes `specflow:develop {NNN-slug}` manually — there is NO auto-resume from scope-change back to develop (auto-resume crosses the user-always-elects line).' (b) R8 addition: 'The impact-list source-section enumeration EXCLUDES the task that triggered the scope-change invocation (when scope-change fires via R2 trigger (a) — the rejected task is the trigger, not an impact). The exclusion is recorded in the impact-list file as a single line in the `## task-history.json` section: `(triggering task T-{N} excluded from impact list — its abort is the precondition for this scope-change run)`.' Then add a corresponding AC sub-clause to AC-2 and AC-8 verifying these contracts.
